page: Amazon Web Services r7a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions and SHA cryptography instructions. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Text processing and single-threaded bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core execution, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, falls into the average tier. A notable hardware tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth: while cached small-block reads and large-block writes perform at average levels, uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 and strong single-core capabilities, this instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is suitable for database operations, in-memory caching, and text processing tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores and DDR5 memory architecture deliver a balanced resource density for memory-bound applications, though workloads requiring high uncached memory read speeds or local storage may experience performance bottlenecks.
